recommendation: Keep the FHIR-12385 audit as-is. If a later run includes Resolved - change required issues, restore MedicationStatement.basedOn and explanatory comments under FHIR-55888 in its own commit rather than reopening this older workflow harmonization issue.
issue_request: FHIR-12385 asked Pharmacy to harmonize MedicationStatement with the Workflow event logical model: keep identifier, code, and status unchanged; rename patient to subject and allow Group; update reason code/reference handling including Observation; add basedOn and context; and add partOf plus effective[x] and dosage wording.
initial_application: The historical source application occurred across ea9a368e150219ed88a5b2d9811443fcdee98cec, which explicitly cited TR#12385 and applied the subject and reason changes; 9445bd2bbd2e405f15219ddd6b7abafec40353a7, which added basedOn and context as workflow elements; and 7003eba639b96a6cb1198300f293effe3f4bda1d, which added partOf plus effective[x] and dosage guidance.
additional_context: MedicationStatement is active in source/fhir.ini and now uses source/medicationstatement/structuredefinition-MedicationStatement.xml as the authoritative source. Current source has the workflow mapping, subject Group support, encounter/context mapping, effective[x] occurrence mapping, reason as CodeableReference including Observation, dosage guidance, and partOf. The current build intentionally lacks MedicationStatement.basedOn: fhir.ini records basedOn as removed, FHIR-32071 recorded a no-change decision after that removal, and FHIR-55888 is a separate 2026 Resolved - change required request to add basedOn back that is outside this default Applied/Published reconciliation scope.
reconciliation: Published an empty audit commit and made no source changes. Re-adding basedOn under FHIR-12385 would bypass the separate FHIR-55888 add-back tracker, while the other FHIR-12385 workflow semantics that remain current are already present.
